elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 affirmatively provides that the Company may participate in any Internet project involving Deerskin Products or substantially similar products; no operative prohibition on competing remains.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 permits participation in any relevant Internet project and states that HDI has no exclusive right to use the “Deerskin” brand, eliminating the original channel and brand exclusivity restrictions.

elements.element: Any restriction on Customer is limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains, so there is no broader product restriction requiring limitation to a named competing product.

elements.element: Any restriction applies only during the term of the Agreement.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains during or after the term.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at a maximum duration of 12 months.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains, so no restriction can extend beyond 12 months.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for Customer’s internal development.
elements.evidence: The unrestricted permission to participate in any relevant project leaves internal development unrestricted; no operative restriction necessitates an express carve-out.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions by Customer.
elements.evidence: No operative non-compete or field-of-use restriction applies to the Company, including through acquisitions, so the condition requiring a carve-out is absent.

result.reason: The redline removes the original project/product non-compete and HDI’s brand-use exclusivity, achieving the preferred position. It therefore also satisfies the fallback’s restriction-limiting conditions because no restriction remains. The term provision and other unrelated language are unchanged. Drafting quality is reduced by the awkward phrase “no exclusive right to use of” and the incomplete Section 6.2 sentence, though the operative intent of Section 6.1 is clear.
